director.chapterArc: False mastery warms into tactical confidence, then collapses at the bridge: Toren mistakes a wind-up for retreat, overrides Milo, and Dessa pays for it. Rook's clinical debrief turns tactical failure into a lesson about status and obedience; Wyck then exposes Toren's deeper habit of assuming authority. The creek scene shifts humiliation into dread as Rook recognizes the disk, suppresses his reaction, and refuses explanation.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder measured and physically grounded. Let the opening irony remain affectionate rather than smug; keep the bridge geography intelligible even at peak violence. Rook's debrief should stay almost entirely in the neutral base—the flatness is the cruelty. Wyck gains force through reasonableness, not volume. Treat the disk recognition as arrested breath and withheld history, never as a theatrical revelation.

cues.delivery: Dry, knowing irony under Toren's self-satisfaction; do not announce the coming punishment.
cues.from: Six days north of Hobb's Wall, Toren had begun to think he was getting good at this, which is the most dangerous thing that can happen to a person.
cues.through: Six days north of Hobb's Wall, Toren had begun to think he was getting good at this, which is the most dangerous thing that can happen to a person.
cues.reason: The opening establishes the dangerous comic gap between Toren's confidence and his actual understanding.

cues.delivery: Dessa's correction is brisk and dry, puncturing pride without cruelty; land “a shape” as practical fact.
cues.from: "Because you've got the only Ember," Dessa said when he mentioned it, in a tone that suggested she thought he was being slow. "Middle's where the reach goes. It's not a compliment, Tor — it's a shape."
cues.through: "Because you've got the only Ember," Dessa said when he mentioned it, in a tone that suggested she thought he was being slow. "Middle's where the reach goes. It's not a compliment, Tor — it's a shape."
cues.reason: A concise status correction foreshadows Toren's later misuse of the middle position.

cues.delivery: A cracked but precise combat call projected over the hounds; preserve every count and direction.
cues.from: "Left!" Milo, up on the cart, cracking. "Left! Six! Six on the left, they're coming across—"
cues.through: "Left!" Milo, up on the cart, cracking. "Left! Six! Six on the left, they're coming across—"
cues.reason: Milo begins performing the exact calling duty on which the line depends.

cues.delivery: Toren calls with the force of certainty, not panic—the dangerous confidence is that he believes he has solved the pattern.
cues.from: "They're off!" he shouted. "They're breaking — they're going to break. They did this before. They're going—"
cues.through: "They're off!" he shouted. "They're breaking — they're going to break. They did this before. They're going—"
cues.reason: His false theory becomes an overriding command.

cues.delivery: Milo's warning breaks through in urgent, directional bursts; fear cracks the voice but never blurs “right.”
cues.from: "Right!" Milo screamed, from the cart. "Right! Right, in the trees, right—"
cues.through: "Right!" Milo screamed, from the cart. "Right! Right, in the trees, right—"
cues.reason: The correct warning must remain unmistakable against Toren's competing call.

cues.delivery: One last full-force directional warning, sharp and isolated rather than prolonged into noise.
cues.reason: This is Milo's final attempt before the fatal turn.

cues.delivery: Make the silent attack more frightening by keeping its physics exact: three trajectories, three impacts, then the abrupt vacuum of sound. No spectacle and no rush.
cues.from: Three hounds came out of the poplars at her in complete silence. They had been getting ready to do it since the first one stopped.
cues.through: The fog closed over the stubble, and the noise stopped, and Dessa was making a sound against the stone.
cues.reason: The hidden flank strikes, Dessa is maimed, and victory drops instantly into consequence.

cues.delivery: Milo's question fails under suppressed dread; keep it small, young, and focused on whether Dessa will live.
cues.from: "Is she—" Milo's voice went. "Is she going to—"
cues.through: "Is she—" Milo's voice went. "Is she going to—"
cues.reason: The first spoken aftermath reveals the group's fear without melodrama.

cues.delivery: Thick with dawning guilt and disbelief; it is an accusation only because Toren cannot yet bear the alternative.
cues.reason: Toren realizes Rook knowingly allowed his mistaken model to survive.

cues.delivery: Wyck is perfectly reasonable, with old resentment held under exact wording. Never raise the voice; let “my whole life” expose the trespass.
cues.from: "You stood in that yard," Wyck said, "and you told that woman we're not staying if he's not. You said it about me. Out loud, to a stranger with a book, about my whole life." His voice was perfectly reasonable, which made it worse. "I never said a word to you about it. You never asked me one. You just — decided, and then you said it, and everybody nodded, because it was Toren, and Toren's dad died, and Toren's got the Ember, so Toren gets to say what all four of us are."
cues.through: "You stood in that yard," Wyck said, "and you told that woman we're not staying if he's not. You said it about me. Out loud, to a stranger with a book, about my whole life." His voice was perfectly reasonable, which made it worse. "I never said a word to you about it. You never asked me one. You just — decided, and then you said it, and everybody nodded, because it was Toren, and Toren's dad died, and Toren's got the Ember, so Toren gets to say what all four of us are."
cues.reason: Wyck reveals that Toren's assumed authority began before the bridge.

cues.delivery: Controlled contempt with pressure accumulating beneath calm syntax. Separate being right from having the right to decide, and keep the final “So” unfinished but firm.
cues.from: "No, she's the one who's bleeding; I'm not the one who's bleeding, so I get to say it." He looked back at Toren. "Maybe you were right. About the yard. I've thought about it, and maybe you were dead right, and I'd be under forty feet of scrap by spring. That's not the thing." He stood up. "The thing is you didn't ask. And tonight you didn't ask either, and Milo told you, and you talked over him, and now she's got a leg that doesn't work. And I'm going to be standing in your line every day for however long this goes on. So."
cues.through: "No, she's the one who's bleeding; I'm not the one who's bleeding, so I get to say it." He looked back at Toren. "Maybe you were right. About the yard. I've thought about it, and maybe you were dead right, and I'd be under forty feet of scrap by spring. That's not the thing." He stood up. "The thing is you didn't ask. And tonight you didn't ask either, and Milo told you, and you talked over him, and now she's got a leg that doesn't work. And I'm going to be standing in your line every day for however long this goes on. So."
cues.reason: Wyck connects the weigh-yard violation directly to Dessa's injury.

cues.delivery: Dessa is thin with pain but still repairing the line; give the instruction practical warmth, not forgiveness or sentiment.
cues.from: "Say it after him," Dessa said, and shut her eyes. "Loud. So they know it's both of us."
cues.through: "Say it after him," Dessa said, and shut her eyes. "Loud. So they know it's both of us."
cues.reason: She establishes a future command structure while holding the damaged group together.

cues.delivery: Slow into uncanny stillness as Toren studies a reaction defined by its absence. Hold the recognition beyond his comprehension; do not imply that he knows what Rook knows.
cues.from: There was no describing it properly, not even to himself, not even as it was happening. The nearest he could get was this: Rook did not react. That was the whole of it. A man walks up on something, and his face does something — surprise, interest, greed, anything — and Rook's face did nothing at all, and everything else about him stopped. His breathing stopped. The hand with the flask in it stopped halfway to being put down. He stood on the gravel four feet away with the lamplight going up under his jaw, and he became, for about three full seconds, an object.
cues.through: Rook's fingers hung there in the air. The disk turned on its cord. Nine fine grooves ran out from the center to the rim, catching the lamp one at a time as it went round, and the man looked at them going past like a man counting something he had counted before.
cues.reason: Rook's arrested body reveals the disk's significance before any explanation is offered.

cues.delivery: Rook's question is stripped of his usual control—not louder or softer, but assembled with effort around an urgent need to know.
cues.reason: This is the first audible fracture in Rook's composure.

cues.delivery: The single laugh contains recognition without amusement. Keep it brief, involuntary, and more alarming for being immediately contained.
cues.through: It was one sound, and there was no humor anywhere in it, and it was the single most frightening thing that had happened to Toren in twelve days that had included three deaths and a road cut full of husks.
cues.reason: Rook's humorless response makes the family saying newly ominous.

cues.delivery: Hard protective urgency with no tenderness. Each prohibition is a practical layer of concealment; the final warning includes Rook himself without self-pity.
cues.from: "Put it under your shirt," Rook said. "Don't take it off to sleep. Don't take it off to swim. Don't show it at a wall, don't show it at a gate, don't show it to a friend and don't show it to me again."
cues.through: "Put it under your shirt," Rook said. "Don't take it off to sleep. Don't take it off to swim. Don't show it at a wall, don't show it at a gate, don't show it to a friend and don't show it to me again."
cues.reason: Rook protects Toren by imposing absolute secrecy while refusing explanation.

cues.delivery: Let certainty arrive coldly and in two clean steps: complete recognition, then complete refusal. No speculative wonder.
cues.from: He set the flask down on the gravel and walked back up the bank, and Toren stayed where he was with the cold running over his hands and the disk lying against his breastbone, and understood two things at once.
cues.through: The second was that he was not going to say.
cues.reason: Toren understands both the depth of Rook's knowledge and the wall around it.

cues.delivery: Observe the sleepless vigil from a distance. Suggest old cost in the stillness without explaining it or softening Rook.
cues.from: Up on the embankment, Rook had not lain down. He was sitting with his back against the cart wheel and the empty road going north in front of him, and he was still sitting there in exactly that position when Toren woke at grey light, and the fire had gone out hours before, and nobody had put it back on.
cues.through: Up on the embankment, Rook had not lain down. He was sitting with his back against the cart wheel and the empty road going north in front of him, and he was still sitting there in exactly that position when Toren woke at grey light, and the fire had gone out hours before, and nobody had put it back on.
cues.reason: The final image carries withheld history into the next morning.
